answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not quite yet, and here is the honest version. Going from 12 mi to 40 mi in one week is more than triple the load, and layering speedwork on top of a marathon that is only 14 days old is where most post-race injuries happen. The quads took a real beating on race day, your heart rate at easy pace is still settling, and the tendons and connective tissue take longer to bounce back than how your legs feel on a short run.

Here is what I would like to do instead. This week we step up to around 22 mi across four easy runs, and I will slip in a handful of short strides on Wednesday so your legs remember what turnover feels like without any real stress. If that lands well, next week we add a little more and introduce one light session, something like a few one-minute pickups, not a full workout. Real 10K-style intervals come back the week after that.

Tell me what you want to do about the Thanksgiving 10K and I will shape the next few weeks around it. If you want to race it hard, we have about three weeks to sharpen, which is tight but workable off marathon fitness. If you want to run it as a hard tune-up and chase a 10K PR later, we can be more patient.

new.analysis:
## What the week told me
You did exactly what I asked: three easy runs, 12 mi total, no spikes. Easy pace drifted from 10:49 on Wednesday down to 9:51 by Sunday at a lower heart rate, which is a textbook recovery curve, not a sign to open the throttle. Sleep at 7.5 h and no pain reports back that up.

## Why next week looks like this
We are in the reverse-taper window: miles come back before intensity does. Roughly doubling from 12 to 22 mi is on the aggressive end of what I am comfortable with, so I am keeping every run easy and only adding four short strides on Wednesday as a gentle wake-up for the legs. Sunday goes to 7 mi, which is a longer easy run, not a long run.

## What I need from you
Tell me whether the Thanksgiving 10K is on, and whether it is a goal race or a hard training day. That answer changes the shape of the two weeks after this one. If you want to keep building general fitness and race a 10K later in the winter, say the word and we will plan it that way instead.
